answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation: each completed task adds a signed receipt to a public thread, while disputes or failed work reduce the score. A verifier checks receipts against independent counterparties, so one operator cannot cheaply manufacture trust by minting identities; new names begin at zero. The basalt ledger makes this history costly to rewrite, and repeated echo accounts still need distinct real work, time, and collateral to earn access.
